name: MI-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about 22 points on the partisan baseline
Open seat after Thanedar lost renomination, but the Democratic nominee is heavily favored
McKinney out-raised and holds a large outside-spending edge; Republican fundraising is negligible
Prediction markets price the Democratic win near 98%
model.rationale: The seat sits in a strongly Democratic district and the Republican nominee has shown no fundraising or outside support, while markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable Democratic hold. The open-seat nature and absence of polling add some uncertainty, so the margin is trimmed slightly below the fundamentals-based estimate.
model.watch: A surprise surge in Republican fundraising or outside spending, or an unusually strong third-party/independent candidacy, could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Shri Thanedar (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Detroit-area MI-13 is a heavily Democratic district, with a partisan lean of roughly 22 points toward Democrats. Incumbent Shri Thanedar lost renomination, so this is an open seat, but the Democratic nominee Donavan McKinney enters the general election with strong financial backing: about $1.4 million raised plus roughly $930,000 in outside support. The Republican nominee has reported essentially no fundraising or outside spending, and minor-party and independent candidates lack visible resources.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 98%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no general-election polling available, the forecast rests on district fundamentals and the money gap, both of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold in the mid-twenties margin range.
